templates.text: Sudden cold touch on sole → sharp leg retraction, full-body startle with a loud, high-pitched cry.
Firm pressure on palm → immediate grasp, followed by a vigorous arm pull and a guttural vocalization.
Abrupt cheek stroke → head turns, mouth roots, and a coordinated suck-swallow-breathe sequence initiates.
Pinprick to heel → explosive cry, contralateral limb flexion, and a rapid withdrawal of the affected leg.
Sudden loss of support → arms fling wide, fingers splay, and a sharp, rhythmic cry begins.
Deep pressure on abdomen → forceful extension of spine, arms thrust forward, and a brief, powerful cry.
Rapid head tilt → eyes widen, arms extend asymmetrically, and a short, staccato cry erupts.
Strong stroking along spine → trunk arches, pelvis lifts, and a sustained, loud wail follows.
Unexpected tap on sternum → gasp, brief apnea, then a cascading cry with full-body tremor.
Restraint of both arms → intense struggling, face reddens, and a rising, crescendo cry is produced.
Vibration on chest wall → cry halts for {seconds} second(s), then resumes with increased pitch and vigor.
Finger pulled from grasp → fingers tighten reflexively, arm flexes, and a short, protesting vocal burst.
Cold stethoscope on back → immediate wriggling escape attempt, followed by a sharp, indignant cry.
Sustained foot squeeze → toes fan, leg extends and kicks, triggering a synchronized cry.
Sudden jostle of bassinet → Moro reflex fully engages, cry onset is instantaneous and loud.
Tug on a single hair → localized flinch, head turn toward stimulus, and a brief, high-frequency cry.
Palmar stroke with texture → grasp, bring-to-mouth movement, and a soft pre-cry vocalization.
Firm rub on the sole → Babinski sign present, leg withdraws, and a short cry is elicited.
Abdominal palpation → grimace, legs draw up, and a strained, grunting cry is released.
Light restraint at shoulders → forceful pushing motion with arms, neck hyperextension, and a loud cry.
Rapid temperature change on skin → gasp, full-body shudder, and a delayed but intense cry response.
Pinch on thigh → targeted limb flexion, contralateral extension, and a sharp, well-defined cry.
Sudden air current on face → breath catch, blink reflex, then a vigorous cry with arm movements.
Deep pressure to plantar surface → toes curl, leg stiffens in extension, and a strong cry is triggered.
Unexpected tap on glabella → blink, brief quieting, followed by a sudden, loud cry outburst.
Restraint during rooting → head turns forcefully, mouth opens wide, and a frustrated cry escalates.
Simultaneous touch to both cheeks → disorganized head movement, arm flailing, and a confused, wavering cry.
Sustained pressure on fontanelle → stilling, then a deep cry with notable respiratory effort.
Vigorous stroking of the eyebrow → eye closure, head turn away, and a soft, whimpering vocalization.
Abrupt change from firm to light touch → startle, limb jerks, and a cry that peaks rapidly in under {seconds} seconds.
